run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The only defect I can substantiate in namespace social-network is a scheduling fault on the jaeger Deployment: it asks for 2 replicas while every replica must attach the single Bound ReadWriteOnce claim jaeger-pvc (openebs-hostpath), and its pod-anti-affinity keeps the two replicas off the same node, so the second replica (pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-kttr7) can never bind a volume and stays Pending/Unschedulable. That is exactly what the platform's own alert rules report firing (PendingPodsDetected, PodSchedulingFailure for social-network/jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-kttr7); the app-tier golden-signal alerts (error rate, latency, request rate, DeploymentNotReady, KubePodNotReady, FailedPodsDetected, PodStatusError) are all inactive. The application tier itself shows no observed failure in the only data available: 26 of 27 Deployments are 1/1 available with 0 restarts, every Service has a ready endpoint, and the sampled traces of the read path (nginx-web-server /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read -> home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service, post-storage-service) are all HTTP 200 with sub-4 ms durations and zero error spans. Two secondary observations are reported but not attributed to the incident: (a) social-graph-service logs a continuous stream of 'GetFollowers user_id: N not found' warnings, which is most consistent with the freshly created, empty social-graph.social-graph collection and no seeded follow data (cold start) rather than a broken dependency, and (b) the jaeger rollout at 17:16:08-17:16:13 restarted the tracing backend, which is why Jaeger's retained history starts at 17:16:11 even though the app started at ~17:16:00. Observation coverage is very thin: Prometheus has essentially no history before 17:14:30/17:16:26, Jaeger only since 17:16:13, nginx access logging is off, and the wrk2 load rounds after 17:16:26 fall outside the authorized window, so no request-level impact of the Pending jaeger replica (or of anything else) could be verified.

claims.text: In namespace social-network, 27 of 28 pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts and start times between 2026-11-21T17:15:58Z and 17:16:04Z; the one exception is pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-kttr7, which is Pending, has no container statuses (no ready flags, no restart counts) and no start time.

Deployment social-network/jaeger declares 2 replicas but reports 1 ready and 1 available replica; all 26 other Deployments in social-network (compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, home-timeline-redis, media-*, nginx-thrift, post-storage-*, social-graph-*, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-*, user-*, user-timeline-*) report 1/1 ready and available.

The ownership chain for the pending pod is Deployment jaeger -> ReplicaSet jaeger-9fd7cdb7c (controller owner Deployment jaeger, uid efaafc0f-1893-4986-8f47-aec014eb78ed), which has spec.replicas 2, readyReplicas 1 and was created 2026-11-21T17:16:09Z.

Deployment jaeger mounts exactly one PersistentVolumeClaim named jaeger-pvc (volume name jaeger-volume) in its pod template, i.e. every replica is configured to attach the same claim, and its container is docker.io/jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.57.

The namespace contains exactly one PersistentVolumeClaim, jaeger-pvc, requesting 1Gi with storageClassName openebs-hostpath and phase Bound; that single ReadWriteOnce claim is the storage resource that is short for a 2-replica deployment.

Pod events inside the window show the jaeger rollout and the scheduling failure: 'Stopping container jaeger' for pod jaeger-7d8548779-f2fs7 at 17:16:08Z; FailedScheduling for pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-kttr7 at 17:16:11Z with '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 2 node(s) didn't find available persistent volumes to bind'; and again at 17:16:13Z with '2 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict'.

The cluster's alerting rules currently report two critical alerts firing for namespace social-network, both on pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-kttr7 and both active since 2026-11-21T17:17:09Z: PendingPodsDetected ('stuck in Pending state') and PodSchedulingFailure ('is unschedulable'); HighRequestErrorRate, HighRequestLatency, HighRequestRate, DeploymentNotReady, KubePodNotReady, PodStatusError, FailedPodsDetected and ContainerCPUThrottling are inactive at that evaluation time.

The sampled traces of the request path in 17:16:11-17:16:24Z are exclusively reads and are successful: nginx-web-server /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read (12 rows, http.status_code=200, 1367-2649 us) and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read (16 rows, http.status_code=200, 1993-3387 us), home-timeline-service read_home_timeline_server 518-797 us, user-timeline-service read_user_timeline_server 1210-2026 us, post-storage-service post_storage_read_posts_server 4-25 us, with error_rows 0 in every span group.

Jaeger's retained traces for this service set begin at 2026-11-21T17:16:11.519Z although the application pods were already running from ~17:16:00Z and the previous jaeger pod was stopped at 17:16:08Z with a new jaeger pod started at 17:16:13Z, so the tracing backend restart is the reason earlier trace history is not retrievable.

social-graph-service logs only 'GetFollowers user_id: N not found' warnings during load: 148 lines matching 'not found' from pod social-graph-service-5b6f86cd77-gpj9d in the 6 minutes ending 17:16:26Z, and 28 such lines between 17:16:09.554Z and 17:16:11.998Z for user_ids spread across 0-999 (e.g. 89, 521, 110, 378, 803, 220, 33, 866).

The social graph store is a brand-new empty database: social-graph-mongodb started at 17:16:01Z with a fresh /data/db and at 17:16:01.874-17:16:01.898Z created collection 'social-graph.social-graph' and built index 'user_id_1'; no social-network pod has an init container that loads seed data and no Mongo pod mounts a PersistentVolumeClaim.

Three services logged MongoDB index-creation failures at startup because their MongoDB was not yet accepting connections - social-graph-service and url-shorten-service at 17:16:00.26-17:16:01.57Z ('No suitable servers found: serverSelectionTimeoutMS expired ... ismaster on social-graph-mongodb:27017' / 'url-shorten-mongodb:27017') and user-timeline-service at 17:16:03.72Z ('user-timeline-mongodb:27017') - and each of them logged 'Starting the ... server' afterwards (url-shorten 17:16:02.6Z, social-graph 17:16:01.89Z).

The load generator pod ran round #0 against http://10.96.24.65:8080/wrk2-api/post/compose from 17:16:09.38Z for 10s and reported '1024 requests in 10.00s', 'Requests/sec: 102.38' and no non-2xx or socket-error line, while its recorded-latency histogram block is empty ('Mean = -nan', 'Max = 0.000, Total count = 0').

Prometheus holds almost no history for this target: count(up) evaluated over the whole 24h authorized window with a 1h step returns a single point at 17:16:26Z, and node_load1 series exist only from 2026-11-21T17:14:30Z onward.

The full metric-name listing returned for this target (737 names) contains only Prometheus/node-exporter/cAdvisor/kube-state-metrics series; no application request, error or latency series (no traces_span_metrics_*, no rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_*, no http_server_request_duration_seconds_*) appeared, so the alerting rules' span-derived golden signals have no data for the social-network services in the observed window.

Service wiring is not visibly broken: all 26 social-network Services are ClusterIP with the ports their clients use (compose-post/home-timeline/user-timeline/post-storage/social-graph/text/unique-id/url-shorten/user/user-mention/media services on 9090, mongodb services on 27017, redis services on 6379, media-frontend 8081->8080) and every Service has exactly 1 ready endpoint address with 0 not-ready addresses.

The monitoring namespace observe is healthy for the scrape path: all 19 pods there (loki-0, loki-gateway, otel-collector, prometheus-server, prometheus-alertmanager, kube-state-metrics, node-exporter daemonset pods, promtail daemonset pods) are Running with 0 restarts.

The root fault originates in Deployment social-network/jaeger: declaring replicas=2 while mounting the single ReadWriteOnce openebs-hostpath claim jaeger-pvc, together with pod anti-affinity that requires the two replicas to sit on different nodes, makes the second replica permanently unschedulable (volume node affinity conflict / no PV to bind), which is the direct reason pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-kttr7 stays Pending and why PendingPodsDetected and PodSchedulingFailure fire for it.

The 'GetFollowers user_id: N not found' stream from social-graph-service is most plausibly the expected cold-start baseline of this freshly deployed, unseeded environment (empty social-graph.social-graph collection created at 17:16:01, no seeded follow edges, no Follow/InsertUser operations observed) rather than a broken dependency, because the same read paths that call this service return 200 in 1-3 ms and no error spans or error-rate alert accompany the warnings; it is nevertheless the only application-tier error-level signal observed and cannot be ruled out as the intended fault without data about a seeded dataset.

A failure of the write/compose path cannot be excluded: POST /wrk2-api/post/compose produced no nginx-web-server spans in the 13 seconds of retained trace data while read endpoints produced 14 traces, and the wrk2 compose round kept an empty latency histogram, which is consistent with compose requests failing before or at nginx; however no 5xx, Lua error, application error log or error alert was observed, so this remains unresolved rather than established.

The single kube-state-metrics scrape at 17:16:26Z is stale and cannot be used as the impact record: it reports pods media-frontend-864dc9bb45-57ft7, nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-66wpv, user-mention-service-56c79c4d9f-wpft2 and user-timeline-service-7779998696-9rj5z as not ready (value 0) / Pending (value 1), while the same pods are Ready in the pod listing taken 3 s later and nginx-thrift and user-timeline-service were demonstrably serving traced requests at that time.

Pod crash / OOM / eviction as the cause is rejected: no pod in social-network has a restart count above 0, no Evicted or OOMKilled event appears in the window, all 26 application Deployments are 1/1 available, and no container is in a waiting reason by the time of the 17:16:29Z pod listing.

Service/endpoint misconfiguration is rejected as the cause: every social-network Service is ClusterIP with the port its clients use and has 1 ready endpoint, and the traced RPCs between nginx-web-server, home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service and post-storage-service completed with 200s in milliseconds.

The startup MongoDB index-creation errors of social-graph-service, url-shorten-service and user-timeline-service (17:16:00-17:16:03Z) are rejected as the cause of the incident: they are container-start races with a not-yet-ready MongoDB, each service logged 'Starting the ... server' immediately afterwards, the collection and index were then created successfully at 17:16:01.87-17:16:01.90Z, and no further error line follows them.

Fix the scheduling configuration of Deployment social-network/jaeger instead of the Pending pod: either set replicas back to 1 (matching the single ReadWriteOnce jaeger-pvc), or give each replica its own openebs-hostpath PVC / a volume that supports multi-attach, or relax the pod anti-affinity (and the node affinity implied by the local PV) so the two replicas can coexist; then delete pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-kttr7 so the ReplicaSet can create a schedulable replacement.

gaps: Change history is not integrated, so I cannot see what changed the jaeger Deployment at 17:16:08-17:16:13Z (old ReplicaSet jaeger-7d8548779 pod stopped, new ReplicaSet jaeger-9fd7cdb7c created with 2 replicas) or who set replicas to 2; the trigger of the rollout remains unknown.

Impact of the Pending jaeger replica on the application is unverified: jaeger is the tracing backend, traces were still being recorded by the single running replica, and no request-level error or latency alert was firing; I could not observe any non-tracing consequence.

No application-level metrics exist for the social-network services in this target: the metric-name listing contains no traces_span_metrics_*, rpc_*, or http_server_request_duration_* series and the alert rules' golden-signal expressions therefore had no data in the observed window; error rate and latency per service are unknown rather than zero.

Prometheus history starts at 17:14:30Z (node_load1) / a single count(up) point at 17:16:26Z and Jaeger's retained traces start at 17:16:11.519Z because the jaeger pod was restarted at 17:16:13Z, so nothing before roughly 17:14 is observable, and the 24h authorized window is effectively empty.

The compose/write path could not be verified: nginx-thrift has access_log off and wrote no stdout/stderr, compose-post-service logged only its startup line, and no compose-post-service span appears in the 13 seconds of retained traces; whether POST /wrk2-api/post/compose returned 2xx or 5xx, and the meaning of the empty wrk2 latency histogram for round #0, remain unknown.

wrk2 load rounds after round #0 (which ended 17:16:19Z; round #1 started 17:16:20Z) and the load pod's later output are outside the authorized window (ends 17:16:26Z), and the wrk2 pod no longer exists, so the load test's final verdict is unknown.

Database contents could not be inspected: secrets are unreadable and no direct MongoDB/Redis querying is available, so I cannot confirm whether the social graph, user store or post store contain any data beyond the empty-collection creation log.

A NetworkPolicy query for namespace social-network returned no objects; that query returning nothing does not prove no policy exists, and no policy-based explanation for any connection failure was therefore checked.
No latency trend could be assessed: with at most a handful of 15s samples from 17:14:30Z onward there is no comparable baseline period for this deployment.
next_steps: Confirm in change history/CI who applied the jaeger Deployment change at ~17:16:08Z and whether replicas: 2 plus the single RWO jaeger-pvc is the intended state.
Review whether pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-kttr7 should be removed by fixing the Deployment (replicas=1, per-replica PVC, or relaxed anti-affinity) and then verify the second replica schedules.

Re-examine application golden signals (per-service error rate and p95 latency from the collector's span metrics) once the span-metric pipeline has data, and compare a healthy baseline before the next load round to decide whether the social-graph-service 'GetFollowers user not found' stream and the empty compose-path histogram indicate a real app-level fault.
Query data from after 17:16:26Z (outside this run's authorized window) for the remaining wrk2 rounds to get the load generator's own success/latency verdict for /wrk2-api/post/compose.

Verify whether the environment is expected to have a seeded social graph (users 0-999 with follow edges) and, if so, restore it; otherwise treat the not-found warnings as expected cold-start behaviour.
